texts.preamble: Pooja @ Seetu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 February, 2026 Author: Milind Ramesh Phadke Bench: Milind Ramesh Phadke Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:6165 1 Mcrc In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Milind Ramesh Phadke On The 17th Of February, 2026 Misc. Criminal Case No. 41032 of 2025 Pooja @ Seetu And Others Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance: Shri Brijesh Kumar Tyagi Ga appearing on behalf of Adv General. Order By invoking inherent powers of this Court, the present petition has been preferred by petitioners under Section 528 of BNSS (482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure) seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.485/2024 registered at Police Station Morar, District Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 140(3) of IPC and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom including Sessions Case No.43/2025, on the basis of compromise.
texts.facts: Order By invoking inherent powers of this Court, the present petition has been preferred by petitioners under Section 528 of BNSS (482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure) seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.485/2024 registered at Police Station Morar, District Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 140(3) of IPC and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom including Sessions Case No.43/2025, on the basis of compromise. As per prosecution story, on 19.08.2024 at about 3:00 PM, the complainant, Saroj Vanshkar (aged 22 years), went to Murar market with her 3-year-old son and 15-day-old daughter. She later went to the fish market across the river, where she met a man and a woman on a motorcycle. After consuming food and liquor with them, she became unconscious. Upon regaining consciousness, both her children were missing, and she suspected NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:6165 2 MCRC-41032-2025 that the said man and woman had abducted them. After searching unsuccessfully, she lodged a report on 20.08.2024. An offence under Section 140(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita was registered and investigated. Alongwith the petition, both the parties have filed I.A. Nos.19311/2025 and 19312/2025 stating therein that the dispute between the parties has been resolved and they have entered into compromise with no intention to pursue the matter further. In compliance of order passed by this Court dated 16.09.2025, the factum of compromise has been verified by the Principal Registrar of this Court, who has recorded the statements of respondent No.2/complainant as well as petitioner/accused and has submitted the report that the parties have arrived at compromise voluntarily without any threat, inducement and coercion. None for the petitioners even in the second round.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the State opposes the petition and submits that the offence alleged against the petitioners is of a serious and heinous nature involving the abduction of two minor children, one aged about three years and the other merely fifteen days old. It is contended that such offences are not private in nature but are crimes against society at large. The mere fact that the complainant and the accused persons have entered into a compromise cannot be a ground for quashing the FIR and consequential NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:6165 3 MCRC-41032-2025 proceedings. It is further submitted that offences under Section 140(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita involve grave allegations affecting public safety and societal interest.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the State opposes the petition and submits that the offence alleged against the petitioners is of a serious and heinous nature involving the abduction of two minor children, one aged about three years and the other merely fifteen days old. It is contended that such offences are not private in nature but are crimes against society at large. The mere fact that the complainant and the accused persons have entered into a compromise cannot be a ground for quashing the FIR and consequential NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:6165 3 MCRC-41032-2025 proceedings. It is further submitted that offences under Section 140(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita involve grave allegations affecting public safety and societal interest.
